entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Vinicius (born unknown, died 46 CE) was a Roman consul twice and grandson-in-law of Emperor Tiberius. As husband of Julia Livilla, he was part of the powerful and influential Julii-Claudian dynasty.

As son and grandson of two consuls, Publius Vinicius and Marcus Vinicius, Marcus Vinicius was deeply connected to the imperial family and the Roman senatorial class. He played a significant role in shaping the Roman Empire's politics and society during the reign of Emperor Claudius.

Marcus Vinicius's legacy is marked by his involvement in the Roman Senate, where he contributed to the governance of the empire. His impact on Roman history is also reflected in his connection to the Julii-Claudian dynasty, which had a profound influence on the course of Roman politics and society.

The sheer scale of the Roman Empire, which at its peak spanned three continents, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Marcus Vinicius and his family.
